Peak M is the molecular ion peak, M⁺. Peak M has a relative abundance fifteen times that of peak M+1.

Peaks M and M+2 are of equal height.

What could be compound X?
items.examiner_comment:
Question 40

The most common incorrect answer was C. Peaks M and M+2 are of equal height, so compound X is a
bromine compound. The correct answer must be C or D. To deduce the number of carbon atoms in a
compound the formula from 22.2.5 in the syllabus is required.100 ÷ (1.1 × 15) gives the answer 6.06, so
there are six carbon atoms per molecule. This confirms the correct answer as D and not C.

J is a branched-chain alcohol, C₅H₁₂O. J is heated under reflux with an excess of Cr₂O₇²⁻ / H⁺ until no further reaction occurs. An organic compound K is formed in good yield.

The infra-red spectrum of K is shown.

items.stem_raw:
J is a branched-chain alcohol, C₅H₁₂O. J is heated under reflux with an excess of Cr₂O₇²⁻ / H⁺ until no further reaction occurs. An organic compound K is formed in good yield.

The infra-red spectrum of K is shown.

What are the structures of the branched-chain alcohol J and compound K?
items.examiner_comment:
Question 30

The most commonly chosen incorrect answer was D. From the infra-red spectrum, K clearly has a C=O
group but no COOH group; it is therefore an aldehyde or a ketone. This rules out D. The conditions stated in
the question would oxidise an aldehyde to a carboxylic acid. Therefore, K is a ketone and J must be a
secondary alcohol. The answer cannot be B as this structure does not have a branched chain. Therefore, the
answer is C.

items.examiner_comment:
Question 1

The most common incorrect answer was D.
The total abundance of the three peaks is 108.3. The sum which gives the A
r is therefore ((100 × 20) + (0.3 ×
21) + (8 × 22)) / 108.3. The answer to this sum is 20.15.

items.stem:
A molecule of an organic compound, P, contains three carbon atoms and shows a strong absorption at 1720 cm⁻¹ in its infrared spectrum.

P is reacted with an excess of hot acidified potassium dichromate(VI) forming organic product Q.

Q shows a strong absorption at 1700 cm⁻¹ and a strong, broad absorption centred at 2800 cm⁻¹ in its infrared spectrum.

bond | functional group containing the bond | characteristic infrared absorption range (in wavenumbers) / cm⁻¹
C–O | hydroxy, ester | 1040–1300
C=C | aromatic compound, alkene | 1500–1680
C=O | amide; carbonyl, carboxyl; ester | 1640–1690; 1670–1740; 1710–1750
C≡N | nitrile | 2200–2250
C–H | alkane | 2850–2950
N–H | amine, amide | 3300–3500
O–H | carboxyl; hydroxy | 2500–3000; 3200–3600

What is P?
